- When sentiment is negative and forecast is trending up, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overshoot — cap forecast at +10% above recent peak for 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, model often overestimates — apply 0.5–1.5% downward bias for 10-day horizon.  
- If sentiment is strongly negative and price is falling, model often underestimates — add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to avoid premature bottoming.  
- Mean reversion bias: if 30-day forecast is >1.5σ above recent 30-day mean, reduce by 0.5–1.0σ for next 7 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is consistently negative over last 5 days, model tends to lag — add 0.3–0.7% upward bias to catch reversal.
